headline: On last trading day, Sensex and Nifty ended lower, snapping a four-week rally amid profit booking.

marketStatus.message: Market is closed today because it is a weekend. It will reopen on Monday, 30 November.

why: Profit booking by investors after recent gains pushed benchmark indices into the red.
Selling pressure in IT stocks dragged down the market indices.
Rising crude oil prices, with Brent crude topping $97, dampened investor sentiment.
Bond markets remained cautious ahead of the upcoming RBI policy announcement.
whatHappening: Sensex and Nifty snapped their four-week winning streak on Friday to close in the red.
In weekly performance, TCS was among the top gainers while Tata Steel lagged.
India-based ACG Capsules announced plans to move production to the US following Trump trade crackdowns.
Tata Sons filed caveats after the Bombay HC refused relief regarding Tata Trusts' plea.
summary:
On the last trading session, Indian benchmark indices Sensex and Nifty ended lower, snapping a four-week winning streak due to profit booking and drag in IT stocks.
Rising Brent crude prices above $97 per barrel and caution ahead of the RBI policy meeting added to market pressure.
Among major stocks, TCS led weekly gains while Tata Steel was among the key laggards.
